## Our data

```{r}
penguins |>

```

```{r}
rosling_tidy <- read_csv(here("data", "rosling_tidy.csv"))
```

---

# 0. One number for the whole table {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Missing values**

---

## The mean of a column

```{r}
penguins |>
  summarize(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g))
```

The result is `NA`. Some penguins have no body mass. R cannot compute a mean with unknown values, so it returns `NA`.

---

## na.rm = TRUE

```{r}
# na.rm = TRUE removes the missing values before the mean
penguins |>
  summarize(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE))
```

One number describes all penguins: 4,202 g. We want one number for each species.

---

# 1. Split, apply, combine {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**One number for each group**

---

## Three steps

| Step | Job | Code |
|------|-----|------|
| Split | Separate the rows into groups | `group_by(species)` |
| Apply | Run a function on each group | `mean(body_mass_g)` |
| Combine | Join the results in one table | `summarize()` |

---

## One mean per species

```{r}
# group_by() splits by species, mean() applies, summarize() combines
penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarize(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE))
```

The result has one row per species. Gentoo penguins weigh over 1,300 g more than the other two species.

---


# 2. Rows behind each mean {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**n() and count()**

---

## How many penguins are behind each mean?

```{r}
# n() counts the rows of each group
penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarize(n = n(), mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE))
```

---

## count() gives the same n

```{r}
# count() splits and counts in one step
penguins |>
  count(species)
```

---

## count() with two variables

```{r}
# One row for each combination of species and island
penguins |>
  count(species, island)
```

Adelie lives on three islands. Chinstrap lives only on Dream. Gentoo lives only on Biscoe.

---

## Your turn 2 {background-color="#d5e8d4"}

```{r}
#| eval: false
penguins |>
  group_by(island) |>
  summarize(n = ___, mean_bill = mean(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE))
```

Answer: [YOUR ANSWER HERE] has the shortest bills.

# 3. Combine the verbs {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**filter, group_by, summarize, arrange**

---

## Females only

```{r}
# filter() keeps the rows, group_by() splits, summarize() combines,
# arrange() sorts the summary
penguins |>
  filter(sex == "female") |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarize(n = n(), mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_mass))
```

---

## Your turn 3 {background-color="#d5e8d4"}

**Males only: the mean flipper length of each species, from the longest to the shortest.**

```{r}
#| eval: false
penguins |>
  filter(sex == "___") |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarize(n = n(), mean_flipper = mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(___(mean_flipper))
```

Answer: [YOUR ANSWER HERE] is first, with [YOUR ANSWER HERE] mm.

# 4. Gapminder {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**A mean of countries or of people?**

---

## Look at the data first

```{r}
rosling_tidy |>
  glimpse()
```

One row for each country and year. `life_exp` is life expectancy in years. `population` is the number of people.

---

## One mean for Asia in 2007

```{r}
rosling_tidy |>
  filter(year == 2007, continent == "Asia") |>
  summarize(mean_life = mean(life_exp))
```

Is 70.7 years the life expectancy of a typical person in Asia?

---

## The countries behind the mean

```{r}
# The three largest countries of Asia
rosling_tidy |>
  filter(year == 2007, continent == "Asia") |>
  arrange(desc(population)) |>
  head(3)
```

```{r}
# The three smallest countries of Asia
rosling_tidy |>
  filter(year == 2007, continent == "Asia") |>
  arrange(population) |>
  head(3)
```

`mean()` gives each country one vote. Bahrain (708,573 people) counts as much as China (1,318,683,096 people). The mean describes countries and misses most of the people.

---

## Fix it by hand: count each person once

```{r}
# Multiply each life expectancy by the population, add them up,
# then divide by the total population
rosling_tidy |>
  filter(year == 2007, continent == "Asia") |>
  summarize(mean_life_people = sum(life_exp * population) / sum(population))
```

A large country adds more to the sum, so it counts in proportion to its people. The result is 69.4 years.

---

## The shortcut: weighted.mean()

```{r}
# The values first, then the weights
rosling_tidy |>
  filter(year == 2007, continent == "Asia") |>
  summarize(mean_life_people = weighted.mean(life_exp, population))
```

The result equals the previous slide: 69.4 years.

---

## All continents, both means

```{r}
rosling_tidy |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarize(
    mean_countries = mean(life_exp),
    mean_people = weighted.mean(life_exp, population)
  )
```

Asia drops from 70.7 to 69.4 years. The Americas rise from 73.6 to 75.4 years.

---

---

## Recap {.smaller}

| Task | Code |
|------|------|
| Ignore missing values | `mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)` |
| One summary per group | `group_by(g) \|> summarize(...)` |
| Rows in each group | `n()` or `count(g)` |
| Count by two variables | `count(g1, g2)` |
| Filter, group, summarize, sort | `filter() \|> group_by() \|> summarize() \|> arrange()` |
| Mean that counts each person once | `weighted.mean(x, weights)` |
